correctness.rationale: Deleting within-shore phases by local unitaries gives amplitudes p^−8 times the cross phase. Tracing the other shore gives entries p^−8 on pairs in the same coset of ker(C^T), zero elsewhere. Each coset contributes one eigenvalue p^−r and there are p^r cosets. I enumerated all 6,435 representatives containing vertex 15, constructed blocks by the three modular edge predicates, and implemented integer Smith reduction using unimodular row/column Euclidean operations, including adding a trailing row when the pivot fails to divide the remaining block. The resulting positive diagonal entries were checked for divisibility and matched all 15 class multiplicities. The only possible prime divisors are 2 and 3; the histograms in rank order 5,6,7,8 are (124,1923,3056,1332) at 2, (189,1851,2892,1503) at 3, and (124,1539,2888,1884) for every p≥5. Exactly one block has factors (1,1,1,1,1,3,3,3); its shores are the two color classes, as all 24 edges cross and the graph is connected. The modular ranks follow by reducing the unimodular transformations, not by extrapolating from a finite prime test.
residual_risks: Prime-dimensional pure, unweighted states and the specified finite graph only; no extension to composite dimensions or noise.

evidence: The generalized Petersen theorem treats a specified alternating-layer cut of each graph.
The all-prime line-graph theorem concerns line graphs; a cubic triangle-free graph cannot be a line graph because each base vertex of degree at least three induces a triangle.
The graph-state papers give general constructions and rank tools, not the evaluated census.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A larger family of graphs with one designated cut is not a broader result for arbitrary balanced cuts. The other all-prime formula does not apply to this host.

evidence: The point–block cut is the alternating u-even/v-odd versus u-odd/v-even cut. Integer cross-block Smith factors determine all prime cut ranks.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Compared both graph presentations and the cut-rank formulation, not merely the graph-state title. A single color-class cut or ordinary adjacency spectrum does not determine these block counts.

value.rationale: A complete integral rank profile of a canonical symmetric incidence graph answers the natural balanced-cut question for every prime, with one compact finite classification. The uniqueness of a three-unit characteristic-three loss across the full population gives information that a single-cut theorem cannot provide. This is a quantitative benchmark for arithmetic sensitivity of graph-state entanglement, not a claim of computing advantage.
residual_risks: Finite benchmark only; does not establish a closed-form census for a general family or a practical resource advantage.
